nodes.name: Carbon cloth pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The piece of carbon cloth (about 2×4 cm) was carefully dealt with acetone, ultra-pure water and absolute ethanol in the ultrasonic bath for 15 min each time. At last, the carbon cloth was vacuum-dried overnight.

nodes.name: Co8FeV@CC Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.56 mmol (0.7450 g) Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.32 mmol (0.1293 g) Fe(NO3)3·9H2O and 0.32 mmol (0.05024 g) VCl3 were dispersed into 35 mL ultra-pure water by stirring for 15 min. Next, 0.3 g urea was added into the above solution after it was transparent. Then, the mixed solution and the pretreated carbon cloth were moved into a 50 mL polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) reaction kettle and heated at 120°C for 12 h. Ultimately, Co8FeV@CC was vacuum-dried after it was cooled down to room temperature.

nodes.name: α-Co(OH)2 Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A block of carbon cloth with the area of ~4 cm² was employed as the working electrode while Pt electrode (2×2 cm) and Hg/HgO electrode were applied as the counter electrode and reference electrode, respectively. The solution consists of 0.02 M Co(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.1 M NH4Cl should be prepared. Then, the chronopotentiometry was used at the constant current density of 5 mA cm⁻² for 1 h to carry out the electrodeposition. Finally, the product was dried overnight at 60°C.

nodes.name: γ-FeOOH Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A block of carbon cloth with the area of ~4 cm² was employed as the working electrode while Pt electrode (2×2 cm) and Hg/HgO electrode were applied as the counter electrode and reference electrode, respectively. The electrolyte solution is composed of 0.1 M FeSO4 and 0.05 M NaNO3. The chronoamperometry was utilized here at the constant potential of 0.8 V (vs. Hg/HgO) for 1 h to conduct the electrodeposition of γ-FeOOH on carbon cloth.

nodes.name: VOOH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol (0.2340 g) NH4VO3 was dissolved in 45 mL ultra-pure water with continuous stirring. Subsequently, 1 mL HCl (1 M) was added into the above solution at a rate of 1 drop per minute during which the solution turned into transparent yellow. Then, 5 mL hydrazine hydrate (85%) was added into the solution with constant stirring and the solution became turbid accompanied with its color changed to gray from yellow. The solution was thereafter moved into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 120°C for 8 h. The sample was washed with ultra-pure water and absolute ethanol for several times after it was cooled off to room temperature, which was followed by the overnight vacuum drying at 60°C.

nodes.name: Drop-casting self-supported electrodes
nodes.procedure: To form a homogeneous ink, 5.0 mg powders were dispersed in a solution consisting of 475 μL absolute ethanol, 475 μL deionized water and 50 μL Nafion (5 wt %) in the ultrasonic bath for 30 min. Afterward, 200 μL catalysts ink was successively dropped on the carbon cloth and then the carbon cloth loaded with catalysts was dried at 60 °C for 2 h. As a result, the mass loading of the above self-supported electrodes was maintained at ~1 mg cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images (Fig. 1b,e) show Co₈FeV@CC nanosheets uniformly and densely anchored on carbon fiber surface with irregular edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FESEM images in Fig. 1b and e display the micromorphology of Co₈FeV@CC. Obviously, its nanosheets are uniformly and densely anchored on the surface of the carbon fiber, however, the specific shape and size of these nanosheets exhibit differences...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.27 nm and 0.38 nm corresponding to (012) and (006) planes of LDH materials; nanosheet thickness ~1.4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) image displayed in Fig. 1c indicates... the distance of adjacent fringes... were measured to be 0.27 nm and 0.38 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping (Fig. 1f) shows uniform Co, Fe, V distribution; EDS spectrum (Fig. 1g) gives Co₈FeV@CC composition Co 81.869 wt%, Fe 8.910 wt%, V 9.221 wt%; molar ratio Co:Fe:V = 7.91:1.02:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping (Fig. 1f) shows that Co, Fe, and V are uniformly distributed... The relative mass fractions of Co, Fe, and V in Co₈FeV@CC were calculated at 81.869%, 8.910%, and 9.221%, respectively. ... The molar ratio of Co:Fe:V is 7.91:1.02:1...

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM image confirms ultrathin Co₈FeV@CC nanosheets with thickness ~1.4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of the monodispersed nanosheet was measured to be approximately 1.4 nm (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Co₈FeV@CC match JCPDS No. 50-0235 for LDHs with diffraction peaks positively shifted ~0.5° compared to α-Co(OH)₂ due to interlayer anions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co₈FeV@CC exhibits a similar crystal structure with Co₄V@CC and Co₄Fe@CC (Fig. 2a), which complies with JCPDS No. 50-0235... the diffraction peaks of LDHs positively shift ~0.5° compared with those of α-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR shows intense NO₃⁻ band at 1500 cm⁻¹ confirming interlayer anions in LDHs; broad band at 3450 cm⁻¹ indicates hydrogen-bonded hydroxyl groups.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2c, the intense bands at 1500 cm⁻¹ are attributed to NO₃⁻... the broad bands around 3450 cm⁻¹ are ascribed to the stretching of the hydrogen-bonded hydroxyl groups...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p shows Co(II) at 777-784 eV, 793-801 eV; Co 2p₃/₂ shifts -0.6 eV vs Co₄Fe@CC due to V; Fe 2p shows Fe(III) with -0.9 eV shift vs Co₄Fe@CC; V 2p₃/₂ shifts +0.4 eV vs Co₄V@CC indicating V electron donation to Co/Fe.
